title: Lesson 2. Nation of shoppers
subtitle: Покупки в Великобритании и Беларуси: High Street, Harrods, ГУМ, Комаровка

sections.title: 1. Shopping in the UK
sections.text: Napoleon once described the British as «a nation of {shopkeepers}». Today they could be called «a nation of {shoppers}», because shopping is the most popular national {leisure activity}. The main shopping street in most towns is called the {High Street}. {Oxford Street} in London is the world's biggest High Street, with more than {100} stores of world-famous {brands}. Most large towns have a {department store} that sells {household goods} and clothing. In London, {Harrods} is the largest department store in {Europe}; it has about {300} departments, including the Christmas department and the {food halls}. For {unique} souvenirs of high {quality}, head to {Covent Garden}, which has street markets, live music and trendy cafes.

sections.title: 2. Shopping in Belarus
sections.text: Belarus has shops of all kinds: large {malls}, {department stores}, {markets} and {fairs}. In Minsk, popular places are the department stores {GUM} and {TsUM} and the shopping centres {Nemiga}, {Stolitsa}, {Dana Mall} and {Arena City}. For more traditional shopping, go to {Komarovsky Market}, one of the oldest food markets in the city. Tourists often buy Belarusian brands known for high {quality}: clothes, shoes, cosmetics, home textiles, sweets and drinks. Well-known chocolate brands are {Kommunarka} and {Spartak}. Traditional souvenirs are {dolls} in national costumes, hand-painted {wooden toys} and spoons, {tablecloths} and napkins.
chain: Nemiga, Stolitsa, Dana Mall, Arena City

sections.title: 3. Words from the text
sections.text: A {High Street} is a main shopping street. A {souvenir} is something you buy to remember a holiday. {Goods} are things you can buy. {Brands} are trade names. {Food halls} are areas in a mall where fast food is sold around a common eating area. Something {of high quality} is very well made. {Unique} means one of a kind. To {head to} a place means to go in its direction.

flashcards.q: Как сегодня можно назвать британцев и почему?
flashcards.a: «A nation of shoppers»: шопинг — самое популярное национальное развлечение.

flashcards.q: Какая улица в Лондоне — самая большая High Street в мире?
flashcards.a: Oxford Street: более 100 магазинов всемирно известных брендов.
Самый большой универмаг Европы, около 300 отделов (в том числе рождественский и food halls).

flashcards.q: Куда ехать за уникальными сувенирами в Лондоне?
flashcards.a: В Covent Garden: уличные рынки, живая музыка, модные кафе и сувенирные магазины.

flashcards.q: Назовите универмаги и торговые центры Минска.
flashcards.a: GUM, TsUM; Nemiga, Stolitsa, Dana Mall, Arena City.
Komarovsky Market — один из старейших продуктовых рынков города.

flashcards.q: Какие шоколадные бренды названы в тексте?

flashcards.a: Куклы в национальных костюмах, расписные деревянные игрушки и ложки, скатерти и салфетки.
